# Summary of the Cairn System Rules

## Basic Pulse (Rule C1)
A pulse makes a cairn grow. The growth has two components: a fixed stride amount plus a variable amount based on how tall the cairn already is. Specifically, you add the stride, then add however many complete stride-sized groups fit into the current height. Taller cairns grow more from a single pulse.

## Repeated Pulses (Rule C2)
When applying multiple pulses in sequence, each pulse must be recalculated from scratch using the new height. You cannot reuse the stride count from an earlier pulse—the proportional growth changes as the height changes.

## Leaks (Rule C3)
A leak is a proportional loss applied after a pulse. For every group of marks equal to the leak size, one mark is lost from the pulsed height. The leak happens in sequence: pulse first, then leak removes marks based on the new height.

## Finding Origins (Rule C4)
You can work backwards from a final height to find the starting height before pulses. Since pulses always accelerate growth in taller cairns, there's only one possible origin. Reverse the pulse operation by solving the equation algebraically rather than simply subtracting.

## Drains (Rule C5)
A drain removes a fixed number of marks after each pulse—unlike a leak which is proportional. The cairn only empties when the drain consistently exceeds what each pulse adds. Cairns can survive many cycles because pulses keep fighting the drain.

## Merging Cairns (Rule C6)
Two cairns combine using shares (fractional weights) and a tether (fixed adjustment). Each cairn contributes a floored proportion of its height, then the tether is added. The result isn't simply adding the heights or averaging them.
